gaps.lead: Perhaps she never received our message.
gaps.explanation: may/might have + participle = possibility in the past.

gaps.lead: There isn't a single clean cup left in the cupboard.
gaps.hint: run out of = have none left
gaps.explanation: run out of = have no more of something left.

gaps.lead: The guidebook says this bridge is Roman.
gaps.explanation: be supposed to be = generally said or believed to be.

gaps.lead: I only understood the pattern much later.
gaps.explanation: Front 'only + time phrase' forces inversion: Only much later did I understand.

gaps.lead: She prefers reading books to watching television.
gaps.explanation: prefer X to Y = would rather do X than do Y.

gaps.lead: The results were announced, and immediately people began celebrating.
gaps.sentence: The results had ___ people began celebrating.
gaps.explanation: No sooner had the results been announced than people began…
